claims.claim: Stealth is described as unviable or poorly implemented because players are forced into unavoidable firefights.

citations.review_text: Metro-esque game. Fun run and gun. However stealth is put on a back foot

Softest of good grades for me here, as I won't be playing this again. First, the good: incredible writing, world-building, visuals, sound design, gunplay, soundtrack/score, and voice acting really carry the day and kept me coming back even when I was frustrated. Maybe because I'm coming off the last two Deus Ex games before this, but I felt like this game struggled with how it wanted to play. There's stealth, but it's not really viable as a strategy because you will run into unavoidable firefights. But run-and-gun isn't that viable either on higher difficulties, and as a cover shooter it's not great. It just doesn't do any of the three combat areas well, though stealth is by far the worst. Also does that thing where the game tells you to go find some tools to fix up the helicopter, but in going there you fall through the floor and end up having to go through a long roundabout sewer system combat just to get back to the base. These obstructions just bogged the game down and didn't add anything to the story. Still, some truly epic sound, visuals, story, and voice acting make this is a recommend. Also: be sure to pay attention to the perks, you will want these in the later missions. Ran smooth as silk for me on Win11, so kudos for that.

Opponents have aimbot, the game pushes you to play stealth and then kills you for it in the last chapter (no strong opponents get killed by stealth shenannigans) the story was nice but very impossible to believe and linear, the feeling of the 60's and the whole world occupied by nazis is quite genuine and nice, but the combat is frustrating to say the least. Oh and the last boss fight? Worst thing you could ever hope for unrewarding as hell and 0 vision, you just have to play peekaboo behind some black pipes for 1 hour straight only to get one very ♥♥♥♥♥♥ ending for all your troubles. Unfortunate Garbage Design besides the worldbuilding.

Wolfenstein: The New Order is a fantastic revival of a classic franchise, effortlessly blending old school, visceral combat with a surprisingly deep, character driven story. The game delivers an alternate history 1960s world dominated by a technologically advanced Nazi regime, making every gunfight feel weighty and thrilling especially when you’re dual wielding heavy weapons or stealthily clearing out rooms with throwing knives. While it suffers slightly from occasional pacing hiccups, a few clunky forced stealth segments, and a minor annoyance in manually picking up scattered ammo, and putting directly in a gunfight after some of the cutscenes with less weapons and ammo, the campaign remains an absolute blast from the beginning to the end. It is a game that respects its roots while establishing a compelling new identity.

Wolfenstein: The New Order is awesome. I enjoyed every bit of it. Completed all achievements as well. On startup, you'll need to adjust some settings to get it running better since it don't like newer hardware.
Open the command menu by clicking " ctrl + alt + ~ " all at once, then type/paste " jobs_numthreads 4 ". It'll prevent your CPU from causing issues such as frame drops in combat. You can also lookup online how to change the resolution to something higher than 1080p as well. Also look up id5Tweaker to play higher than 60 FPS.

9/10
Great story, affordable, amazing artstyle.

The 60fps cap cannot be fixed, which is a minus.

Utterly ridiculous, but awesome at the same time. Great writing, charismatic chararacters, and just a ton of fun. I was annoyed at the locked 60 FPS for the first 15 minutes, but then I just forgot about it and just had fun.

Some technical limitations--it's hardcapped at 60 fps & sometimes the game chooses to open on the wrong monitor--but overall still holds up. Gunplay is punchy and responsive. Cutscenes, worldbuilding and story are all well-crafted.

Oh and don't enter the vents in the Berlin Catacombs (Chapter 10), Blazkowicz [b]will[/b] get stuck.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game suffers from bugs where collectibles like enigma files disappear or achievement progress items glitch.

citations.review_text: If you are a completionist, avoid this game. Bugs cause enigma files to disappear.

Interesting game, TBH.
Although by 2026 standards this game has a lot of minor problems and small bugs that overall do add up to be noticeable nothing that really drags the game too much.
All weapons have 2 types of ammo to make things varied, since you play against soldiers, enemy variety is always going to be thin, so the different ammo do help in this endeavour.
The perk system is something that really makes the game a lot better while you play it, more ammo, better reload, a lot of upgrades come from these perks after you make the necessary requirements. Some are blocked and that is really annoying, but other than that it was a good way to make the game more varied in a very stale genre.
The story of this game is absolute perfection from a pitch point of view: "You're a Nazi killer in a Nazi controlled world... just go ham!" Every situation can be used to kill Nazis since they are the world now. But from an execution POV feels a bit flat after such a strong start.
When you get to the middle point, the city that had cameras everywhere now does not see helicopters being stolen or where they were hidden, same when the Nazi war machine loses one of the state of the art U-Boats, life continues like nothing happened which is more unlikely than BJ surviving all the wounds suffered after the coma. Clearly the thought about the stages first and how they connect each other later.
The World is something I wish I could see more, because the Nazis actually documented what they envisioned the future to be, so like the London reformed architecture to fit Nazi inspired ones is something that only this game in a timeline like this can create, but it gets fantastical too fast.
Overall the game has a comic book super hero in a comic book world where everything reverts back to the same status quo until the end.
Good game, good fun.

actually it's a fun and entertaining game with some nice gameplay ideas.

but as usual there are a few problems.
movement feels really sluggish and while the magic invisible walls will prevent most unfortunate accidents you will miss the occasional stairs or fall off a ledge. especially noticeable and annoying during heavy combat when you are looking for cover or the next medkit and tiny boxes, chairs and even door frames turn into deathtraps as you get stuck on them.

the whole theme feels strangely off. it very obviously doesn't take itself serious on countless occasions. at the some time other parts are really  dark and grim. this fits neither style and feels like the game tries to sit on both chairs at the same time.

there are loads of collectibles to hunt down and grab (if you care enough) but like in many other games basically all levels are cut into distinct areas. once that door closes you are not going back in case you missed something. come on! why can't i explore freely?

stealth gameplay feels rather weak and in many cases it's not possible at all. it's a [i]wolfenstein[/i] game after all so you can't really complain about that but if you sneak too much early you lack practice and unlockable combat perks for when the sh!t really hits the fan later.


finishing the game took 18 hours and a good part of that time went into hunting secrets and unlocking combat perks via challenges.
25 hours in total for 100% achievements.

pro tip: use headphones so your neighbours don't hear gunshots, screaming and "he1l h1tler" in the middle of the night.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the narrative as blending serious, emotional character writing with an absurd alternate-history setting.

citations.review_text: Wolfenstein: The New Order is the standard for what a modern shooter should be. Guns feel exceptional and distinct, the narrative is somehow both cartoonishly over-the-top and heartbreakingly serious, and there are collectibles galore for the collectathon sickos. The length (15ish hours) felt just right for a single playthrough, though there are two narrative paths and multiple difficulty options to enhance replayability. The worldbuilding was highly compelling and I found myself getting lost reading the in-game notes and listening to the audio logs. It's obvious how much care and attention the developers at MachineGames gave to this series, and I truly hope we haven't seen the last of it.

I love everything about this game! it's gun play is fast paced and offers excellent challenge. It's storytelling is great and knows how to balance seriousness and comedy. I had a great time exploring the levels looking for secrets. the world building and detail is immaculate, and they do not hold back with the cruelty of the Nazis, leaving me no shortage of motivation to kill them in all sorts of ways from silently killing them with a knife to firing two underbarrelled rocket launchers at the same time! Truly I had a blast 100%ing this game

one of the best shooter campaigns of all time, bombastic, emotional, and incredibly cinematic. The attention to detail in all regards is impressive, the art design, the voice acting, the staging and cinematography in the cutscenes, it's all impressive even today. Then there's the shooting, visceral, over the top and infinitely gratifying. Combine that with a surprisingly fun stealth system and this game never fails to be fun. My only complaint is that the story gets a little goofy towards the end, which is a shame when the rest of the game manages to have a shockingly serious and emotional tone despite the over the top world and set pieces, makes the goofy plot points at the end feel even more out of place. However, despite that I think the actual ending of the game is fantastic. If you haven't played it, then you should, it's an experience worth having. (also the sound track is by Mick Gordon, so that's a bonus too!) If you do play it, check out the idtweaker mod, it's very easy to install and can really help with performance and visual clarity as the engine this game runs on is kinda wack.

I was much too harsh on this game when it released. I had a very narrow idea of what Wolfenstein should be and how our main protagonist should act.

12 years later: New Order is just a fun joyride that knows when to take itself serious and when to lean into the pure absurdity of the world its created that makes for some genuinely funny moments.

citations.review_text:
Beat this game on the highest difficulty and did not have a good time.

Game is presented super well with lots of good, unique and unsettling visual design. It's just glowing with characters that I really was rooting for.

The writing is above what I expected, which is necessary considering this game series is pretty politically uncomplicated and this game in particular seems to take a relentlessly bleak outlook of a post-WW2 world. It's still not good enough for me not to feel this game is an insensitive mess. It's not a COD campaign, but it's definitely not as good as I was led to beleive.

Unlike something like Wolfenstein 3D, this game 's straight-foward gameplay seems incongruent with how much effort they dedicate to the narrative. I know this game is meant to be kitschy or whatever, but that ♥♥♥♥ is not working for me. 

The actual "game" part of this game sucks, like it's so annoying to have to spray enemies for mags on end when sometimes all it takes is half a second for them to end you. Not to mention the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ final boss who bascially doesn't take any damage unless you use the 3 weapons he's weak to. 

Spending 2 minutes listening to the sombre credits after firing at a mech suit for 5 whole minutes bascially solidified how I feel about this game. You spend ages spewing bullets into overly-tanky enemies, then you see a overly serious cutscene. 

This game is like the most 6/10 thing I've ever played. 
When I remember who reccomeneded me this game, they're getting it.

TLDR; Is The New Order worth playing in current year? Yes if you're wanting a conclusion to The Old Blood game. A fun time and continuation of BJ's Nazi Killing Spree and with more ways to kill for extra fun!

Combat/Stealth gameplay is pretty consistent here just as with The Old Blood (given the fact it came out before that game). The gun sounds are pretty nice and beefy, energy weapons are zappy and the melee is pretty good for the most part, so long as you hit the enemies at the right time. The game can be considered easier with stealth though in some sections either stealth or full on combat can be just as fun and easy. However with UBER difficulty it ramps up the challenge and makes things more interesting, unlike the UBER difficulty in The Old Blood.

Story is decent for what it is. The fact that it doesn't shy away from the horrors of a world living with the horrible Nazis and their concentration camps. Just makes killing the bastards in all manner of ways all that more fun. For a game that came out during 2014, it holds up decently well all things considered. The characters are interesting enough to carry you through the story and the villains are overly evil, sometimes evil for sake of evil (But remember, they're nazis so evil is what they are). The final boss was pretty fun and a proper challenge. Far as I see it, The Old Blood and The New Order are two stories that fit well and end that arc well. Didn't really need a sequel with New Colossus in my opinion given the ending of this game.

I will say though, I could do without the sex scenes in my shooter game.  Felt out of place and didn't really need to see it to know BJ was tied to another character romantically. Though take it or leave it, I'm just happy you can skip the cutscenes after loading is done, which is pretty fast on modern hardware.

Wolfenstein: The New Order — Achievement Hunter Review

🕒 Time played: 20 hours
🏆 Completion: 100% game completion + all Steam achievements

As an achievement hunter, I completed Wolfenstein: The New Order 100% in 20 hours, unlocking every Steam achievement.

Overall, I really enjoyed the game. As a shooter, it feels great — the gunplay is satisfying, the action is intense, and the gameplay stays fun throughout the entire experience. The story was also surprisingly good and kept me interested from beginning to end.

For my 100% playthrough, I started collecting all the letters, gold items, and Enigma codes right from the first chapter. If you plan on completing the game fully, I highly recommend doing the collectibles as you progress instead of leaving everything for the end.

Another important part of the achievement list is the perk system. There are achievements tied to getting kills in different ways, such as specific weapon kills, stealth kills, and other combat-related challenges. My advice is simple:
if you find a good farming spot, use the checkpoint system and start grinding there. The progress saves, so you can easily farm perks within a single chapter without replaying the whole game repeatedly.

I also highly recommend saving the UBER difficulty achievement for your final playthrough. If you complete the last chapter on UBER difficulty, after the credits you’ll unlock all lower difficulty achievements as well, which saves a lot of time.

From an achievement hunter’s perspective, the game is very manageable and not overly difficult to complete at 100%.

Excellent gunplay and combat
Strong story and atmosphere
Fun perk and progression system
Reasonable achievement difficulty
Collectibles are easy to track if done early

Some perk grinding required
Collectibles can be missed easily
Replay needed for cleanup if not planned properly
